Sell2Rent is a fast-growing residential real estate platform specializing in sale-leaseback transactions. We help homeowners unlock their home equity without moving, while connecting properties with single-family rental investors. We operate in 30+ states and have closed 200+ transactions.
Technology is a key driver of our growth. We’ve built a proprietary operating platform, AI agents for lead qualification and outreach, an investor-matching layer, and a lead engine that supports our sales process.
We’re looking for a Chief Technology Officer (CTO) who sees technology as a growth and revenue engine - not just an engineering function. You’ll work closely with Sales, and Marketing, to use AI, automation, data, and product to generate more qualified leads, improve conversion, accelerate the sales cycle, and close more transactions.
You’ll inherit real, revenue-generating technology, a talented team, and the opportunity to create the technology strategy that will help Sell2Rent scale faster and sell more.
If you’re excited about using technology to drive measurable business results, this is your opportunity to make a major impact.

What you'll own

Technology strategy. You set the direction: architecture, build-vs-buy, which platforms we standardize on, where AI is a genuine advantage and where it's a distraction. You'll be the person in the room who knows what's actually possible and what it costs.

The engineering organization. You lead a distributed team of roughly ten across engineering and data, all of them in Latin America. You'll grow it, structure it, and set the bar.

Scaling the platform. Our twelve-month mandate is to ship the roadmap and scale what we've built - completing the migration off legacy systems, hardening the platform, and getting to a place where the business can grow transaction volume without engineering becoming the bottleneck.

The AI layer. Agents handle a meaningful share of our qualification, outreach, and internal operations today. Deciding how far that goes - and building it so it's a durable advantage rather than a demo - is one of the most interesting problems here.

Resilience and continuity. Security, access governance, vendor management, monitoring, documentation, and the discipline that ensures no single person is ever again the only one who knows how something works. We've learned this lesson the expensive way and we're not repeating it.

Executive partnership. You sit on the Executive Committee. You'll work directly with the CEO and the sales, marketing, and operations leaders - translating what the business needs into what gets built, and telling us honestly when what we're asking for is a bad idea.

• You find blind spots. Much of the value in your first six months is telling us what we don't know we're missing - in our architecture, our tooling, our security posture, and our process.

title: RFP: Human Resource Subject Matter Lead
company: New Left Accelerator and The Capacity Shop
description:
About NLA and TCS

New Left Accelerator (NLA) and its 501(c)(3) affiliate, The Capacity Shop (TCS), lead operational capacity-building programs that empower social justice organizations and movements to execute bold work safely. We bridge the gap between ambitious strategy and operational excellence, scaling structures and impact without sacrificing legal compliance or integrity. To achieve systemic change, organizations must use every tool in their toolbox effectively-including multi-entity structures.

Through deep collaboration with field experts, we build the financial and compliance training systems that allow movement organizations to manage risk and remain resilient. Our work is rooted in a commitment to:

•
Power Building For Systemic Change: Equipping organizations to build power to dismantle oppressive structures.

•
Operational Power: Building the "operational" capacity to execute bold work and to strategically manage risk.

•
A Multi-Entity Lens: Optimizing the diverse legal structures necessary to win critical battles.

•
Transformative Partnerships: Prioritizing those working at the intersections of race, gender, and class.

At NLA, our work is guided by a Theory of Change. We accompany organizations and movements in building sustainable, resilient ecosystems prepared to win the most ambitious fights of our time.

Overview of Project

Background

NLA and TCS develop training on a range of operations topics, focused on what multi-entity organizations need to know. We are developing foundational content for a training module for HR staff at mid-size, multi-entity social justice organizations that do election-year work. The content will focus on the HR issues specific to these organizations when they hire for organizing positions during an election cycle and then end those positions afterward.

Scope of Work

The HR Subject Matter Lead will work under the direction of the TCS, Senior Director of Training and Curriculum to develop a four-part, role-based education module for HR specialists. The module will:

• Apply a nonprofit multi-entity Human Resources lens throughout

• Apply a social justice lens to HR in the organizing and election year context

• Build on existing NLA/TCS content

• Incorporate NLA's learning frameworks and practices

• Be customizable for state content

Deliverables and Outcomes

December 2026 through June 2027

•

title: Accounting Clerk (Accounts Payable / Accounts Receivable)

Accounting Clerk (Accounts Payable / Accounts Receivable)

About the role:
We are seeking a detail-oriented Accounting Clerk to join our Accounting team. This role focuses on Accounts Payable and Accounts Receivable, on vendor and dealer administration. You will manage vendor billings and dealer invoices, and ensure all expenses are accurately recorded and reconciled. You will play a key role in maintaining accurate financial records in Accounts Payable and Accounts Receivable, supporting month-end close, and strengthening internal controls.
The purpose of the Accounting Clerk is to efficiently manage the processing of vendor invoices for Accounts Payable, as well as generating invoices to dealers in Accounts Receivable. This position supports the day-to-day financial operations of the business, ensuring timely and accurate postings.

What are we looking for?

• Experience with accounting and general ledger entries a must

• Ability to speak fluent English

• Ability to read and write in English

• Strong attention to detail

• Computer

• Great multitasker

What you’ll Do

Accounts Payable

• Accurately and timely processing of invoices on a daily basis with the correct GL CODE.

• Maintain up to date Vendor records (maintain and organize digital records)

• Process all online bills for monthly payment (hydro, utilities, internet, Waste Connections, etc).

• Assist with month-end closing process by ensuring monthly invoices are posted before cut off.

• Reconcile monthly account statements from vendors to ensure invoices posted in the system match

• Assist in any accounting related activities, including year end audit, as required.

Accounts Receivable

• Process daily Shipping Manifest to generate the Invoice by Date Report and Sunroom Reports.

• Post Dealer Invoices into Xero Retail and Xero Manufacturing

• Generate monthly Account Statement to Dealers and manage collection & communication activities

• Assist with month-end transactions and reporting.

• Maintain organized digital records

• Support administrative and communication tasks within the AR function.

• Assist in any accounting related activities, including year end audit, as required.

What’s in it for you?

• ₱355 to ₱445 Philippine Pesos (PHP) per hour

• Experience within a rapidly growing company

• Remote work

title: Product Cost Management Lead - AI Infrastructure
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization is building the infrastructure foundation for frontier AI systems. The Supply Chain organization enables scalable, resilient, and efficient supply chains across custom silicon, systems, networking, memory, storage, and rack-scale infrastructure.

Our team connects engineering, supplier strategy, manufacturing, planning, deployment, and finance to make hardware cost, supply, and execution tradeoffs clear from early architecture through production and sustaining operations.

About the Role

OpenAI is seeking a Product Cost Management Lead to own the official costed bill of materials (BOM), system and cluster cost and price baseline, and platform-to-platform total cost of ownership (TCO) for our 1P AI infrastructure. You will turn component, system, POD, manufacturing, deployment, DC, service, and lifecycle inputs into a trusted view of product economics that informs technical and business decisions, including transition timing.

You will partner with Engineering, Strategic Sourcing, Manufacturing-partner management, Finance, Planning, Supply Chain Program Management, Operations Program Management, and infrastructure teams to evaluate engineering / design changes, compare alternatives, identify cost-reduction opportunities, and track realized benefits.

This is an individual contributor role with broad cross-functional ownership. The ideal candidate combines hardware cost expertise, rigorous modeling, sound judgment, and the ability to explain complex tradeoffs clearly to engineering, operations, and senior leaders.

In this role, you will:

- Own the official costed BOM and system/pod roll-up by platform, generation, configuration, build phase, volume, and mix. Maintain version control and traceability to quotes, source owners, assumptions, and engineering revisions.

- Publish and maintain the system/pod cost and price baseline, reconciling component pricing and manufacturing-partner inputs with approved configurations and planning assumptions.

- Build platform-to-platform TCO comparisons covering component content, non-recurring engineering, tooling, manufacturing labor and overhead, yield, scrap, test, logistics, deployment, housing and site costs, power and cooling, networking, spares, service, warranty, and lifecycle costs.

- Partner with housing and site teams to integrate their cost inputs into product economics, documenting scope, timing, allocation assumptions, and gaps so platform comparisons are consistent and avoid double counting.

- Quantify the cost impact of engineering change orders and notices (ECOs/ECNs), architecture, specification, configuration, and qualification changes before approval. Assess recurring and one-time costs, implementation timing, inventory exposure, and expected benefits.

- Develop a prioritized cost-reduction, value-engineering, and second-source opportunity funnel with Engineering, Strategic Sourcing, and manufacturing-partner management. Evaluate qualification costs, investment, payback, supply improvements, and execution risk.

- Analyze actual, forecast, quoted, committed, and purchase-price costs against the baseline. Explain material variances, identify root causes, and track recovery actions with accountable owners and dates.

- Build sensitivity and scenario analyses for supplier and manufacturing-partner options, capacity, volume and mix, yield, configuration, site, deployment timing, and lifecycle tradeoffs. Present clear recommendations with assumptions, confidence ranges, and decision deadlines.

- Validate savings and cost avoidance with Finance and accountable source owners. Distinguish identified opportunities, approved actions, and realized benefits, including offsets and implementation costs.

- Establish cost-data definitions, BOM hierarchy, allocation methods, currency and volume assumptions, refresh expectations, and change-control processes. Flag stale, incomplete, or unsupported inputs before they affect decisions.

We're hiring a Head of Engineering to lead engineering for one of our product tribes. You'll manage 15 to 20 engineers directly, with tech leads in each squad owning technical direction but no management layer between you and the team. You report to the CTO and sit in a tribe leadership trio with the Product Tribe Lead and Design Lead. Which tribe you'd lead is something we'll work out with you during the process.

This is a people leadership role with a hard technical requirement. The engineers report to you, so hiring, development, performance and pace are yours. At the same time you have to hold your own on system architecture: challenge estimates from your engineers, spar with the Product Tribe Lead on solutions, and know when a design is wrong before it ships. This role needs both.

HOW WE'RE SET UP

Tribes are the organisational body: people management, capacity, planning and reporting live there. Squads are assigned to problem spaces and run discovery and delivery, each led by a trio of Tech Lead, Product Manager and Product Designer. Tech Leads own the technical decisions in their squad, including estimates, and write code alongside their engineers. They don't manage people. You do.

We keep the structure deliberately flat. Management is anchored at tribe level, squad composition flexes to serve the most important work, and structure changes as we learn (roughly every six months in practice, not on a schedule). Discovery and delivery run in parallel: the next mission is scoped before engineers finish the current one, so engineers weigh in on architecture early and have the context to unblock themselves.

- Feasibility and delivery for the tribe. You're accountable for tribe-wide delivery outcomes and velocity: the right problems, solved at the right quality, as fast as possible.

- Technical judgement across squads. Broad understanding of the tribe's systems and how they fit into the wider Moss architecture. You challenge estimates and technical proposals from your engineers; you don't produce the estimates yourself.

- A seat in the tribe trio. Roadmap and planning input through a feasibility lens. You argue solutions and trade-offs with the Product Tribe Lead as a technical peer, and push back on scope and timelines when the engineering picture says so.

- Operating rhythm. How the tribe plans, estimates, tracks and reports on delivery, with proactive, timely transparency to the tribe and to leadership, the good and the bad.

- Capacity. Putting your best people on the most impactful work, moving engineers between squads (and, where it serves Moss, between tribes) while still letting people build real domain depth.

- Alignment across tribes. Tribe leads aren't isolated trios. You align proactively with your peer Heads of Engineering and with platform and architecture owners, and you resolve shared-architecture questions through alignment, not around it.

HOW WE EXPECT LEADERS TO OPERATE

- Velocity first, with high agency. Working smart and hard on the right problems.

- Lead by example, stay close to the work. You know the details of what your team is building and course-correct in real time. You get hands-on when speed or quality is on the line.

title: Revenue Enablement Manager (m/f/d), Just-in-Time Enablement
description:
SoSafe has the ambition to become the leading human risk management provider in Europe. Our award-winning awareness platform triggers behavioural change by providing effective and engaging training and simulations on cybersecurity and data protection. Cybercrime is costing the world >$10 trillion annually and growing by 15% p.a. - we invite you to be part of the solution!

ABOUT THE ROLE

Every month, something new reaches our field teams from Product, Product Marketing and Marketing: a new use case, a fresh sales narrative, a campaign, a product update. Too often it arrives as a Slack post or a long deck, and sellers never really pick it up.

As Revenue Enablement Manager, Just-in-Time Enablement, you own that last mile. You are the front door between the teams who create news and the teams who use it, and you make sure every launch reaches Sales, Customer Success and Partnerships across Europe at the right time, in a format they can use in their next conversation.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

- Run the launch intake. Be the single entry point for PMM, Product, Marketing and others who want something to reach the field. Prioritize with clear criteria so sellers aren't overloaded.

- Own the field release calendar. Keep one view of what's coming, when, and for whom, shared with creators and sales managers.

- Turn launches into what sellers need. Shape each release into: what's new, who it's for, why customers care, how to talk about it, and how to handle the likely questions.

- Coach the creators. Brief PMM, Product and Marketing on what the field needs and review their materials before they go out. When the input is raw (specs, messaging docs, long decks), write the enablement content yourself: short, clear and practical.

- Deliver just in time. Pick the right format and moment: a 20-minute live session, a short recording, a one-pager, a talk track. Not so early it's forgotten, not so late it's useless.

- Make it stick. Run practice sessions, give managers simple talking points, and check that sellers can explain the new thing in their own words.

- Check it landed. Track attendance, usage in calls and deals, and rep feedback. Share what you learn with the creators so the next launch is better.

- Keep one home for launch material. Everything findable in one place with an owner and a review date; retire what's outdated.

- Hand over to curriculum. Work closely with your colleagues in the revenue enablement team, who fold a launch into the regular training once it is no longer new. Agree what moves over, when, and in what form, so nothing is built twice.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

- 5+ years in revenue enablement, product marketing, sales training or a similar role in B2B SaaS, ideally at a scaleup.

- Experience rolling out launches, messaging or campaigns to sales teams, with examples you can share.

- Ability to explain a product use case or sales narrative simply, and to spot what a seller really needs from it.

- Strong stakeholder skills: you can say "not this month", ask for a 3-slide version of a 40-slide deck, and keep the relationship strong.

- Well organized: you juggle several launches at once and hit dates.

- Clear writing and confident live facilitation.

- Hands-on with LMS, AI, video editing tools, a CRM and call recording tools, and a habit of using data to check adoption.

- Fluent English and German.

NICE TO HAVE:

- Background in product marketing or product management.

- Experience with security, compliance or HR-related products.

- Familiarity with a structured sales methodology such as SPICED or MEDDICC.

HOW SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE:

First 30 days: learn

- Meet the leads in PMM, Product, Marketing, Sales and Customer Success. Learn how launches reach the field today and where they get lost.

- Review the last 3-5 launches: what reached the field and what stuck.

- Agree which upcoming launches come first and who owns what, intake process and readiness gates.

Days 31-60: set up and pilot

- Start the launch intake

The role sits close to DX Engineering and is fully focused on content. You’ll work directly with the Head of Developer Experience, the DX team, Render’s docs owners, and external content partners.

title: Staff Fraud Strategy Analyst
description:
Relay is fundamentally reshaping how goods move in an online era. Backed by Europe’s largest-ever logistics Series A ($35M) led by deep-tech investors Plural, and a recently closed Series B ($95M), Relay is scaling faster than 99% of venture-backed startups. We're assembling the most talent-dense team the logistics industry has ever seen

Relay’s Mission is to free commerce from friction. Today, high delivery costs act as a hidden tax on e-commerce, quietly shaping what can be sold online and limiting who can participate. We envision a world where more goods move more freely between more people, making the online shopping experience seamless and accessible to everyone.

THE TEAM
• ~160 people, around half in engineering, product and data
• 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research
• Thousands of data points captured, calculated, analysed and predicted for every single parcel we handle
• An intellectually vibrant culture of first‑principles thinking, tight feedback loops and relentless experimentation

Relay delivers 400,000 parcels a day through people who don't work for us: van drivers who choose their own shifts, local shops that hold parcels, and couriers who take them to the door. We went from 3,000 parcels a day in London to 400,000 across the UK in under three years.

Parcel delivery has a quality problem the industry has learned to live with. Parcels go missing between depots. Parcels get marked as delivered and never reach the customer. Most carriers treat a steady rate of loss as a cost of doing business. Relay is building the delivery company where that stops being true.

That is harder for us than for most, because nearly everyone who touches a Relay parcel is an independent partner. We can't manage them into performance. We have to build the standards, the evidence and the product that make doing the job well the natural outcome. Engineering builds the product changes you design.

PARTNER EXCELLENCE HIGHLIGHTS

- You own decision-making, not the model: you decide which signals count, which checks become rules, and whether each fix belongs in product, policy or training. The squad lead acts on your calls.

- Most of a parcel's journey happens between scans. How do you prove a handover happened without making the job slower for the people doing it?

- A delivery is marked complete and the customer says it never came. How do you tell a wrong address from a handover that went wrong, and put the fix where it belongs: product, policy or training?

- Some checks can only answer "can't tell". Which are worth making provable, and which should we stop measuring?

- A whole area, not a slice: you decide what evidence a whole network runs on, and the result is on the street the next morning.

- Analytics at the front, not in support: the squad's roadmap follows the analysis, in a data team of about 30 across analytics, operational research and data science.

THE OPPORTUNITY

As a Staff Fraud Strategy Analyst at Relay, you'll:

- Decide which Partner Excellence problems are real and which only look real, before anyone builds a fix.

- Design how Partner Excellence decides: which signals count, what evidence the network runs on, and what good looks like.

- Tell the squad lead what to change and what to stop, and get a decision.

- Build the thing that decides: data applications, monitors and alerts, not decks, using Claude and agents to ship your own tools.

- Go and look when the data and the street disagree: the sort centre, the van, the shop.

- Get the missing data built, and prove which fixes worked. In a year, the squad can prove every handover in the network.

WE'RE LOOKING FOR CANDIDATES WHO…

- Have owned fraud, risk or trust decisions end to end: turned investigations into rules, standards or interventions, and owned their number, such as the false positive rate you were held to, rather than building the model.

- Have run investigations in fraud, risk, financial crime or trust

Bask Health provides a full-service SaaS platform that enables doctors, entrepreneurs, and healthcare businesses to build, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses.
We're an entrepreneurial, product-focused team that values ownership, speed, and exceptional execution. We work in small teams, tackle complex problems, and expect everyone to take an active role in building and improving our products.
About the Role
We're looking for a Product Manager, Data & Intelligence / BaskQL to help build and improve the data and analytics experiences across Bask's telehealth platform.
You'll work on BaskQL and related data intelligence capabilities, helping merchants and internal teams access, understand, and use information about their businesses and platform operations.

title: Senior iOS Developer - Swift, Kotlin Multiplatform & AI Coding
description:

Employment: Full-time, long-term position
Start date: As soon as possible after selection and agreement
Salary: Based on experience, technical expertise, and level of responsibility
About Us
We are developing a mobile application that combines real-world interactions with location and proximity technologies. Our team uses AI coding tools and autonomous coding agents to accelerate development, improve our engineering workflows, and build practical knowledge across the team.
We are looking for a senior developer who can take ownership of iOS development, deliver reliable software, and help our team become more effective at building applications with AI.
Job Description
We are seeking an experienced Senior iOS App Developer with an excellent background in native iOS development using Swift and SwiftUI, together with practical experience integrating Kotlin Multiplatform into iOS applications.
This is a hands-on engineering role. You will develop and improve our iOS application, integrate shared application logic, solve complex technical problems, and establish effective workflows for AI-assisted and agentic development.
Experience with GPS, Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), Ultra-Wideband (UWB), or related location and proximity technologies would be particularly valuable.

• Mentor our junior team member through practical demonstrations, pair programming, and clear explanations.

• Support application signing, release preparation, and distribution through TestFlight and the App Store.

• Demonstrated senior-level experience delivering and maintaining production iOS applications.

• Excellent practical knowledge of Swift, SwiftUI, and the iOS development ecosystem.

• Practical experience with Kotlin Multiplatform and its integration into native iOS applications.

• Solid understanding of application architecture, asynchronous programming, lifecycle management, and state management.

• Strong debugging skills across application code, shared modules, APIs, and device behavior.

• Substantial hands-on experience using AI coding tools to deliver working software.

• A strong interest in agentic coding and the ability to establish effective development workflows around coding agents.

• The ability to assess AI-generated solutions critically and explain technical decisions.

• Willingness and ability to teach less experienced team members patiently and clearly.

• The ability to work independently, communicate progress clearly, and take ownership of results in a remote team.

title: MSK Teletherapy Physical Therapist / PTA — Lees Summit, MO
description:
Treat PeteDME’s MSK Integrated Care patients from home. Our program pairs knee and lumbar bracing with physical therapy and remote therapeutic monitoring, delivered through a network of in-home therapists. Remote visits and monitoring are paid per visit and per call.

How you join
Every therapist on the remote caseload starts with six in-person brace fittings on patients from your own current caseload, so you know the devices you will be coaching patients on. Each fitting is a paid clinical visit - intake, fitting, and follow-up - at a flat fee agreed in writing before your first patient. We give you a one-page screening tool to identify candidates among the patients you already see, and we handle the prescription, benefit verification, and the paperwork.

This is not a sales role. We do not ask you to refer; you treat patients you already see.

After six fittings
Teletherapy patient referrals from PeteDME begin: our patients, work from home, on your schedule, paid per visit and per call.

What you get
• Free specialized training and certification in orthopedic bracing.
• AI-generated SOAP notes - no new EMR to learn.
• Keep your current job. This is additional, independent-contractor work alongside it.
• Flat fees fixed in advance; no part of your pay depends on volume or on referrals.
Requirements
• Active physical therapist or physical therapist assistant license in the state where you practice.
• Currently working in home health or another in-home setting.
• You evaluate and provide treatment.

How to apply
Complete the short questionnaire. It asks about your license, your setting, and your caseload, and it asks you to acknowledge that teletherapy referrals begin after six fittings. A clinical onboarding specialist will reach out within one business day.

title: Senior Pharmacy Practice Professional
description:
Become a part of our caring community

Join a team dedicated to shaping pharmacy practice on a national scale. As a Senior Pharmacy Practice Professional, you will serve as a subject matter expert on Prescription Monitoring Program (PMP) requirements, pharmacy regulations, and operational best practices across all 50 states. This highly visible role combines independent research, complex problem-solving, and cross-functional collaboration to support compliant operations, resolve shipment discrepancies, and advance pharmacy practice standards that enhance the member experience. The Senior Pharmacy Practice Professional defines, implements, and maintains pharmacy practice standards that support compliant pharmacy operations across the organization. This role serves as a subject matter expert on pharmacy laws, regulations, and Prescription Monitoring Program (PMP) requirements, ensuring external regulatory requirements and internal standards are current, consistently applied, and effectively communicated. Working independently with minimal oversight, the Senior Pharmacy Practice Professional researches and analyzes complex regulatory and operational issues, investigates shipment discrepancies, verifies legal and compliance requirements, develops policies and guidance, and collaborates with cross-functional teams to support operational excellence and influence departmental strategy. This remote position requires strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills, with no travel required.

Use your skills to make an impact

Required Qualifications

• Licensed Pharmacy Technician in your state of residence OR National Pharmacy Technician certification (PTCB or ExCPT)

• 3+ years of experience interpreting and applying pharmacy regulations, compliance requirements, or professional practice standards

• 3+ years of experience conducting regulatory research, analyzing complex issues, and developing operational recommendations

• Experience communicating regulatory requirements and business impacts to cross-functional stakeholders

• Demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects and priorities independently with minimal supervision

Preferred Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Healthcare Administration, Business, Public Health, or a related field

• Experience supporting Prescription Monitoring Program (PMP) compliance activities

• Experience within a PBM, health plan, specialty pharmacy, mail-order pharmacy, or other pharmacy operations environment

• Experience developing pharmacy policies, procedures, or professional practice standards

• Six Sigma, Lean, or Project Management Professional (PMP) certification
